title: Unit 16 Gases (part 1)
textbookText: Circle the correct alternative of the following questions.
1. What products are formed on heating of limestone to a high temperature using coal?
i) methane and limestone ii) lime and carbondioxide
ii) Acetylene and carbondioxide iv) Ammonia and lime
2. Which of the following statements is true?
i) Carbondionde is collected in the gas jar by the upward displacement of air.
ii) Carbondoride is collected in the gas jar by the downward displacement of air.
iii) Carbondioxide is collected in the gas jar by the upward displacement of water
iv) Carbondioxide is collected in the gas jar by the downward displacement of water.
Ans:- ii) Carbondoride is collected in the gas jar by the downward displacement of air.
3. Which compounds are formed when carbon dioxide gas is passed through lime water for some time?
i) Calcium bisulphate ii) Calcium bicarbonate iii) Calcium sulphate
4. In what ratio should ammonium chloride and calcium hydroxide be mixed for the laboratory preparation of ammonia gas?
Ans:- ii) upward displacement of air

1. Write the chemical formula of limewater.
Ans:- The chemical formula of limewater is Ca(OH)₂.
2. Which gas is used for making blue print of maps?
Ans:- Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is used for making blueprints of maps.
3 Name two chemicals which are required to prepare carbondioxide gas in laboratory.
Ans:- Two chemicals required to prepare carbon dioxide gas in the laboratory are CaCO₃ and HCl.
4. Which gas is obtained by reacting lime store and dilute hydrochloric acid ?
Ans:- Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is obtained by reacting lime stone and dilute hydrochloric acid.

6. Name two chemicals that are required to prepare ammonia gas in laboratory.
Ans:- Two chemicals required to prepare ammonia gas in the laboratory are NH₄Cl and Ca(OH)₂.
7. Write the molecular formula and molecular weight of ammonia.
Ans:- The molecular formula of ammonia is NH₃ and its molecular weight is 17 g/mol.
8 What is the percentage of carbon dioxide in atmosphere?
Ans:- The percentage of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is about 0.03–0.04%.

9. What is formed if carbon dioxide is cooled to-76°C? Ans:- If carbon dioxide is cooled to −76°C, dry ice (solid CO₂) is formed. 10. Write one use of dry ice. Ans:- One use of dry ice is preservation of food or biological samples. 11. Write one application of green house gases. Ans:- One application of greenhouse gases is keeping the Earth warm by trapping heat. 12. What is meant by acid rain? Ans:- Acid rain is rainwater mixed with acids like H₂SO₄ and HNO₃ formed from air pollution. 13. Write any two example of green house gases. Ans:- Two examples of greenhouse gases are methane (CH₄) and carbon dioxide (CO₂). 14. Write a chemical reaction to show the effect of acid rain on the earth. Ans:- A chemical reaction showing the effect of acid rain: H₂SO₄ + CaCO₃ → CaSO₄ + CO₂ + H₂O. 15. Carbon dioxide can be collected in an open glass jar. Why? Ans:- Carbon dioxide can be collected in an open glass jar because it is denser than air and does not mix quickly.
